svg.title: Smell: what a receptor reads
svg.desc: Left: the settled reading of one orb against distance, with the lowest reading anywhere on the floor when every orb of the world smells at once. Right: the reading after the orb is eaten, at three distances. All values from odour.rs, noise-free.
svg.text: Smell: what a receptor reads, from odour.rs
bound_fraction(c) = c / (c + K): 0 is no odour, 1 is every receptor bound. Noise-free means; the counting noise is under 1% here.
distance from the orb's centre, metres (log scale)
lowest reading anywhere on the floor,
every orb of the world summed
seconds after the orb is eaten
One orb, eaten at t = 0: the trace lingers, then fades
The open issue, made visible: alone, one orb reads 0.96 at a body length and 0.5 at a decay length - a usable gradient.
But every orb smells at once: at the default density the floor never reads below 0.44 (median 0.89); 43% of readings are 0.9 or more.
